blocks.content: Panchayati Raj is the system of local self-government aimed at building democracy at the grass-roots level in rural India.

rows: Includes all adults registered in the electoral rolls of the village
Direct democratic body at grassroots level
Accountable directly to the Gram Sabha

items: Rajasthan was the first state to establish Panchayati Raj, inaugurated in Nagaur district on October 2, 1959.
The normal tenure of a Panchayat is 5 years, and fresh elections must be conducted within 6 months of its dissolution.
Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) originally recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Panchayati Raj was constitutionalized through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992.
The Act added Part IX and the 11th Schedule containing 29 functional items to the Constitution of India.
It establishes a three-tier system: Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zilla Parishad at the district level.
Gram Sabha serves as the foundational body consisting of all registered voters residing within the village area.
A mandatory reservation of not less than one-third (33%) of the total seats is provided for women across all levels.
